recorded.pass:q-blank-field-switch:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blank-field-switch:a: Directly refuted: 'A case doesn't narrow T. Inside case Setting.Port p the setting must be a Setting<Integer>, so a generic parse through a switch looks as if it should work' and then the compile error.
recorded.prompt:q-blank-field-switch:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blank-field-switch:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blank-field-switch:b: Refuted by the example, not by a stated rule: the page's parse switch covers all three records and still fails with 'Integer cannot be converted to T'. The heading 'Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases' supports this.
recorded.prompt:q-blank-field-switch:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-blank-field-switch:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-blank-field-switch:d: 'A switch over the records with no default is checked for coverage', the describe example compiles without default, and 'Leave it out on sealed types'. Caveat: describe takes Setting<?>, not Setting<T>. For the Setting<T> parse example the page reports only branch-value errors, so the refutation for a T-typed selector is by implication.
